subdomain: 1.2 Design end-to-end architectures (input → processing → output → feedback loops)

en.question: An extraction service uses schema-constrained JSON responses to feed a purchase-order importer. Orders must also pass catalog and quantity checks. Refusals and output-limit termination are possible. Which processing-to-output boundary is appropriate?

options.text: Handle completion exceptions, validate the returned record, and apply business checks before importing an order.
options.note: Structured generation does not eliminate documented refusal or truncation cases, and schema validity does not establish catalog membership or acceptable quantities.

options.text: Import every response that parses as JSON, then use the importer's error report to identify invalid business content.
options.note: Parsing alone does not enforce the expected structure or business rules. Deferring validation can allow a malformed or unauthorized business record into the downstream system.

options.text: Use strict tool inputs instead of JSON responses and treat matching tool arguments as approval to create the order.
options.note: Constrained tool inputs regulate structure, not catalog correctness or authorization to import. Moving the schema boundary does not remove the business validation requirement.

options.text: Retry interrupted generations and import the first complete response without repeating catalog or quantity validation.
options.note: A retry can restore a complete response but does not establish semantic validity. Each candidate order still needs the required business checks.
